title: kv-cache: improved eviction + spillover defragmentation heuristics to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Improves KV cache eviction and spillover defragmentation heuristics to reduce memory fragmentation and paging; lowers tail-latency under memory pressure and reduces spillover I/O.
description: Motivation: Under mixed-size key/value workloads we observed increased memory fragmentation and higher-than-expected spillover I/O, leading to p99 latency spikes during memory pressure windows. This PR implements size-aware eviction plus an opportunistic defragmentation worker and smarter spillover batching to reduce fragmentation, defer paging, and lower tail latency. Summary: 1) Size-aware eviction policy that prefers evicting small, high-reuse items to free contiguous regions; 2) Defragmentation manager that coalesces adjacent free regions and relocates resident KV entries in low-priority background passes; 3) Spillover write coalescing and page-aligned spill thresholds to reduce IOPS; 4) Metrics, knobs, and a feature flag for staged rollout. Design details: eviction policy now tracks per-bucket free-run statistics and per-entry size buckets to inform eviction scoring. When fragmentation_ratio = fragmented_bytes / total_free_bytes exceeds defrag_threshold (config default 0.32) the defrag manager schedules defragmentation on an internal low-priority executor that respects SLOs by yielding after max_cpu_micros. Defrag relocations are batched and pinned to a relocation window so they do not interfere with foreground KV access. Spillover path now aggregates small spill writes into page-aligned batches and defers spills under transient pressure for a configurable grace_period_ms to allow reclaims. Backwards compatibility: all changes are behind runtime-config flags and default to safe conservative thresholds. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor KV fragmentation, spill bytes/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates; then 50% and full rollout if no regressions. Metrics added: kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.defrag_runs, kv.relocated_bytes, kv.spill_coalesced_writes, kv.spill_io_bytes. Benchmarks: internal e2e workloads show average spill I/O reduced by ~38% and p99 latency improved by ~12% on mixed-size trace derived from production (see bench results in this PR). Risks and mitigations: relocation can increase transient memory usage; we cap concurrent relocation bytes and provide a hard stop when available_memory falls below emergency_watermark. Follow-ups: tighten heuristics, add per-tenant tuning, and extend to reserved-capacity optimizations.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial size-aware eviction scoring; defrag manager implementation and tests; spillover coalescing and page-alignment writes; metric and config plumbing; integration tests and benchmark harness; fix race in relocation path; tune defaults based on bench results.
review_comments: Diego: Can we avoid moving hot entries during defrag? Author: Defrag uses LRU-heat gating and a relocation score to avoid recent-access items.
Lina: We saw a flaky test in CI on the first run. Author: Fixed race by adding a relocation semaphore and re-ran CI.
Tomás: Consider exposing defrag backoff based on tenant-level SLO. Author: Added a follow-up in ENG-3477 to evaluate per-tenant knobs.
notes: Hotfixable via feature-flag. Default thresholds tuned conservatively. Observability added to detect regressions.
